lessons.0.slides.1.title: 📋 Assessment Scope
lessons.0.slides.1.content:
This comprehensive assessment covers every module in the Level 1 course:

• M1 Introduction to Burgundy
• M2 Terroir and Grape Varieties
• M3 Exploring Côte de Nuits
• M4 Exploring Côte de Beaune
• M5 Chablis In-Depth
• M6 Introduction to Beaujolais
• M7 Côte Chalonnaise and Mâconnais
• M8 Vintages and Prestigious Estates

The bank contains 72 questions; the system randomly draws 20. Passing score: 80 or above.
lessons.0.slides.2.title: 🎯 Key Review Points
lessons.0.slides.2.points.0: Geography and sub-regions: six regions from north to south — Chablis, Côte de Nuits, Côte de Beaune, Côte Chalonnaise, Mâconnais, Beaujolais
lessons.0.slides.2.points.1: Classification tiers: Régionale 53%, Village 36%, Premier Cru 10%, Grand Cru only 1%
lessons.0.slides.2.points.2: Core varieties: Pinot Noir for red, Chardonnay for white; Beaujolais uses Gamay
lessons.0.slides.2.points.3: Côte de Nuits: 24 Grands Crus, Gevrey-Chambertin has the most (9); DRC holds Romanée-Conti and La Tâche as monopoles
lessons.0.slides.2.points.4: Côte de Beaune: 6 white-wine Grands Crus (the Montrachet family); Meursault has no Grand Cru but top-tier Premiers Crus
lessons.0.slides.2.points.5: Chablis: Kimmeridgian oyster-fossil soil, a single Grand Cru AOC containing 7 Climats, classic pairing with oysters
lessons.0.slides.2.points.6: Beaujolais: carbonic maceration, 10 Crus, Moulin-à-Vent earns the title "king of Beaujolais"
lessons.0.slides.2.points.7: Reading labels: village name alone = Village; add 1er Cru = Premier Cru; vineyard name alone = Grand Cru
lessons.0.slides.2.points.8: ⚠️ Scoring 80 or above on this assessment unlocks the Level 2 Intermediate course
